title: Bo Horvat named New York Islanders captain: Why he was the right choice
content:
The New York Islanders named Bo Horvat their captain Monday. The center replaces Anders Lee, who signed with Utah in free agency after eight years wearing the “C.”

The 31-year-old Horvat had 31 goals and 57 points in 68 games last year for the Islanders. He also won an Olympic silver medal with Team Canada. He’s been with the Islanders since January 2023, when they acquired him from Vancouver.

Horvat was previously the Canucks’ captain and has 881 games of NHL experience, plus 34 more in the playoffs. He’s entering the fourth year of an eight-year, $8.5 million average annual value deal.

Horvat is respected around the league and has plenty of leadership experience, which made him a clear candidate for the captaincy after Lee signed in Utah. He spent 3 1/2 seasons as Canucks captain and was an alternate captain under Lee. He plays a responsible style that earned him a spot on Team Canada and is one teammates can emulate.

Star defenseman Matthew Schaefer is the face of the Islanders, but he’s still only 19. Naming Horvat captain ensures Schaefer is not thrust into too big a role too soon.
